stem: In Valmiki's Ramayana, who leads the building of the bridge to Lanka?
options: Angada, the young son of Vali
Nala, the son of Vishvakarma
Jambavan, the king of the bears
Sushena, the father of Tara
why: Nala, son of the divine craftsman Vishvakarma, offers to build the bridge, and the monkeys and bears finish it under him in five days. Valmiki Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda 22.

es.stem: En el Ramayana de Valmiki, ¿quién dirige la construcción del puente hacia Lanka?
options: Angada, el joven hijo de Vali
Nala, el hijo de Vishvakarma
Jambavan, el rey de los osos
Sushena, el padre de Tara
es.why: Nala, hijo del artesano divino Vishvakarma, se ofrece a construir el puente, y los monos y los osos lo terminan bajo su guía en cinco días. Ramayana de Valmiki, Yuddha Kanda 22.

stem: In the traditional (vulgate) text of Valmiki's Ramayana, which hymn does the sage Agastya teach Rama just before his final battle with Ravana?
options: the Shiva Tandava, on Shiva's cosmic dance
the Vishnu Sahasranama, a thousand names
the Gayatri mantra, a Vedic verse to Savitr
the Aditya Hridayam, in praise of the sun
why: In the traditional text, Agastya comes to the battlefield and teaches the weary Rama the Aditya Hridayam, 'the heart of the sun', telling him to recite it before fighting. Valmiki Ramayana (vulgate), Yuddha Kanda 105; the Baroda Critical Edition moves it to an appendix as a later addition.
source: Valmiki Ramayana (vulgate), Yuddha Kanda 105; appendix in the Baroda Critical Edition

es.stem: En el texto tradicional (vulgata) del Ramayana de Valmiki, ¿qué himno le enseña el sabio Agastya a Rama justo antes de su batalla final con Ravana?
options: el Shiva Tandava, sobre la danza cósmica de Shiva
el Vishnu Sahasranama, los mil nombres de Vishnu
el mantra Gayatri, un verso védico a Savitr
el Aditya Hridayam, un himno en alabanza del sol
es.why: En el texto tradicional, Agastya llega al campo de batalla y le enseña al cansado Rama el Aditya Hridayam, 'el corazón del sol', y le pide recitarlo antes de luchar. Ramayana de Valmiki (vulgata), Yuddha Kanda 105; la Edición Crítica de Baroda lo pasa a un apéndice como añadido posterior.

stem: In Valmiki's Sundara Kanda, after finding Sita, why does Hanuman decide to wreck Ravana's ashoka grove?
options: to test the enemy's strength and be brought to Ravana
to carry out Sugriva's order to ruin all Ravana's gardens
to light a signal the army across the sea could see
to answer Sita's request to frighten her guards away
why: With his task done, Hanuman weighs the four means of statecraft (conciliation, gifts, division, force), decides only force will work on the rakshasas, and wrecks the grove to gauge their strength and reach Ravana. Valmiki Ramayana, Sundara Kanda 41.

es.stem: En el Sundara Kanda de Valmiki, después de encontrar a Sita, ¿por qué decide Hanuman destrozar el bosque de ashokas de Ravana?
options: para medir la fuerza del enemigo y ser llevado ante Ravana
para cumplir la orden de Sugriva de arruinar los jardines
para encender una señal visible para el ejército al otro lado
para atender el pedido de Sita de asustar a sus guardias
es.why: Con su misión cumplida, Hanuman sopesa los cuatro medios de la política (conciliación, regalos, división y fuerza), concluye que con los rakshasas solo sirve la fuerza y destroza el bosque para medir su poder y llegar ante Ravana. Ramayana de Valmiki, Sundara Kanda 41.

stem: In Valmiki's Ramayana, when Vibhishana asks Rama for refuge and the camp argues, what vow does Rama state?
options: to judge Vibhishana only after the war has been won
to accept him once he has fought against Ravana
to protect all who come once and say 'I am yours'
to shelter only those who share his own royal line
why: Rama vows to give safety from all beings to anyone who comes to him even once and says 'I am yours', even Ravana himself; Sri Vaishnavas treasure the verse as a teaching on sharanagati, taking refuge. Valmiki Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda 18.

es.stem: En el Ramayana de Valmiki, cuando Vibhishana le pide refugio a Rama y el campamento discute, ¿qué voto declara Rama?
options: juzgar a Vibhishana solo después de ganar la guerra
aceptarlo una vez que haya luchado contra Ravana
proteger a quien venga una vez y diga 'soy tuyo'
dar refugio solo a quienes sean de su linaje real
es.why: Rama promete dar protección frente a todos los seres a quien acuda a él aunque sea una vez y diga 'soy tuyo', incluso al mismo Ravana; los sri vaishnavas atesoran este verso como enseñanza sobre sharanagati, tomar refugio. Ramayana de Valmiki, Yuddha Kanda 18.

stem: Two rival clans have fought for years, and one clan's leader has just been killed. A storyteller cites what Rama tells Vibhishana in Valmiki's Ramayana: enmity ends at death. What does that principle call for?
options: leave his body unburied as a warning to allies
allow quiet rites for him, without any honors
honor him only once his clan admits its wrongs
give his body full funeral rites with honor
why: When Vibhishana hesitates to cremate Ravana, Rama says enmity ends at death and has him given a king's funeral rites. Valmiki Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda 111.

es.stem: Dos clanes rivales llevan años peleando, y el líder de uno acaba de morir. Un narrador cita lo que Rama le dice a Vibhishana en el Ramayana de Valmiki: la enemistad termina con la muerte. ¿Qué pide ese principio?
options: dejar su cuerpo sin sepultar como aviso a sus aliados
permitir ritos discretos, sin ningún honor para él
honrarlo solo cuando su clan admita sus culpas
darle a su cuerpo todos los ritos fúnebres con honor
es.why: Cuando Vibhishana duda en cremar a Ravana, Rama dice que la enemistad termina con la muerte y hace que reciba los ritos fúnebres de un rey. Ramayana de Valmiki, Yuddha Kanda 111.

stem: In Valmiki's Sundara Kanda, why is Hanuman horrified just after setting Lanka on fire?
options: he fears the fire may have burned Sita herself
he sees that Vibhishana's house has caught fire
he recalls that Rama had forbidden any burning
he finds that his own tail cannot be put out
why: Hanuman suddenly fears he has burned Sita and condemns his own anger, until voices in the sky tell him she is unharmed; Vibhishana's house he had deliberately spared. Valmiki Ramayana, Sundara Kanda 54–55.

es.stem: En el Sundara Kanda de Valmiki, ¿por qué Hanuman se horroriza justo después de incendiar Lanka?
options: teme que el fuego haya quemado a la propia Sita
ve que la casa de Vibhishana ha empezado a arder
recuerda que Rama había prohibido quemar nada
descubre que no puede apagar su propia cola
es.why: Hanuman teme de pronto haber quemado a Sita y condena su propia ira, hasta que unas voces en el cielo le dicen que ella está a salvo; la casa de Vibhishana la había respetado a propósito. Ramayana de Valmiki, Sundara Kanda 54–55.

stem: In Valmiki's Sundara Kanda, how does Hanuman get past Surasa over the ocean, and why does his way of doing it matter?
why: Surasa, sent by the gods to test him, demands that he enter her mouth; Hanuman shrinks to the size of a thumb, darts in and out, and so keeps her condition and his mission without a fight, and she blesses him. Valmiki Ramayana, Sundara Kanda 1.

rubric.point: Says he makes himself tiny, enters her mouth and comes straight out. Saying only that he grows larger than her does not count.

Says this fulfils Surasa's condition that he must enter her mouth, so he passes without fighting her and without abandoning his mission. 'He outsmarts her' with no mention of keeping her condition counts as partly.
Mentions that the gods sent Surasa to test his strength and wit, or that she blesses him afterward (optional, strengthens).

es.stem: En el Sundara Kanda de Valmiki, ¿cómo logra Hanuman pasar a Surasa sobre el océano, y por qué importa su manera de hacerlo?
es.why: Surasa, enviada por los dioses para ponerlo a prueba, exige que entre en su boca; Hanuman se reduce al tamaño de un pulgar, entra y sale rápido, y así cumple la condición de ella y su propia misión sin pelear, y ella lo bendice. Ramayana de Valmiki, Sundara Kanda 1.

stem: In the Uttara Kanda as traditionally transmitted, the seventh book of Valmiki's Ramayana, what does Rama do to Sita, and why has this part of the story long been debated?
why: In the Uttara Kanda as handed down, Rama, hearing public gossip about Sita's time in Ravana's house, sends her, pregnant, into the forest, where she bears Lava and Kusha at Valmiki's hermitage. Its justice to Sita has been argued over for centuries and later poets reworked or left out the ending; many modern scholars also consider the book a later addition, while much of the tradition receives it as Valmiki's. Valmiki Ramayana, Uttara Kanda 43–49.

rubric.point: Says Rama sends Sita (pregnant) away to the forest because of what people say about her time in Ravana's house. Mentioning only Lava and Kusha, without the exile, counts as partly.

Gives a reason it is debated: the exile is hard to square with Rama as the ideal king and husband, or with justice to Sita; noting that many scholars doubt the book belongs to the earliest poem also counts. The answer need not take any side on who wrote the book.
Mentions later tellings that reshape or omit the ending, such as Bhavabhuti's Uttararamacharita reuniting the couple or Tulsidas's Ramcharitmanas leaving the exile out (optional, strengthens).

es.stem: En el Uttara Kanda tal como se ha transmitido tradicionalmente, el séptimo libro del Ramayana de Valmiki, ¿qué hace Rama con Sita, y por qué esta parte del relato se ha debatido tanto tiempo?
es.why: En el Uttara Kanda tal como se ha transmitido, Rama, al oír los rumores del pueblo sobre el tiempo de Sita en la casa de Ravana, la envía embarazada al bosque, donde da a luz a Lava y Kusha en la ermita de Valmiki. Su justicia con Sita se discute desde hace siglos y poetas posteriores reelaboraron u omitieron ese final; muchos estudiosos modernos consideran además que el libro se añadió después, mientras que buena parte de la tradición lo recibe como obra de Valmiki. Ramayana de Valmiki, Uttara Kanda 43–49.
